title: Personal Credit Cards: Interest Calculation, Grace Period and Interest Reversals
content:
Interest on Personal Credit Cards is calculated with the average daily balance method, new transactions included, and is worked out separately for four balance types: purchases, cash advances, balance transfers and any penalty-rate balance. Each balance type accrues at its own APR divided by 365 for each day. At statement close, every balance type whose interest comes to more than 0.00 USD is billed as its own interest charge.

## Accrual by balance type

| Balance type | When interest starts |
|---|---|
| Purchases | none for a cycle whose preceding statement was cleared in full by that statement's due date; in any other cycle, from each purchase's posting date |
| Cash advances | from the posting date, with no grace period |
| Balance transfers | at the introductory APR up to and including the introductory end date, and at the purchase APR after it |

The previous statement counts as paid in full when the payments, merchant credits and dispute credits posted from that statement's closing date through its due date add up to at least that statement's balance.

## Smallest interest charge

Where a cycle bears some interest but its total across balance types falls short of the tier's smallest interest charge, the smallest interest charge is billed instead, and it is booked against the purchase balance type.

## Reversing interest

- **Residual interest as a courtesy.** Interest billed on the statement that follows a statement balance paid in full, covering the stretch from that earlier statement's closing date to the day the payment arrived, may be reversed in full as a courtesy. A courtesy reversal of this kind is possible only where the statement balance it follows was in fact paid in full, as the bank's records show. The number of such courtesy reversals is limited by the tier's allowance, counted across all of the customer's cards within the rolling 365 calendar days that end on the current date, that date included.
- **Interest billed in error.** Interest charged at a rate, or on a balance, that this charter does not allow is reversed on the bank error ground, with no limit on how often.
- Any single interest charge can be reversed only once.

## Worked example (hypothetical figures)

A purchase balance averaging 1460.00 USD over a 30-day cycle at an APR of 18.25 percent accrues 1460.00 USD multiplied by 18.25 percent, divided by 365, for each of 30 days: 0.73 USD a day, or 21.90 USD for the cycle. If the only interest in a cycle came to 0.40 USD on a tier whose smallest charge is higher, the smallest charge would be billed in its place and recorded against purchases.
